Mapping the Global Health Landscape: Analysis of Fourteen International Organizations

2026-09-08 Jennifer Kates, Adam Wexler (KFF) global health, international organizations, mapping, architecture reform, LMICs, MOPAN, Lusaka Agenda, WHO
Read the source article

Quick summary

KFF published a descriptive mapping of 14 key global health institutions to inform discussions about duplication, synergies, and architectural reform in the global health ecosystem.

Key takeaways

  • KFF mapped 14 key global health and related international institutions, focusing on their work in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
  • The mapping examines mandates, governance models, financing structures, and operational approaches across organizations
  • Multiple reform efforts are underway: the Lusaka Agenda, the Accra Reset, and WHO's Joint Process on Reform of the Global Health Architecture
  • The mapping is descriptive, not evaluative — it does not assess organizational performance or effectiveness
  • The report is intended to inform discussions about synergies, coordination, duplication, and comparative advantage across entities
